title: Owls Can't Move Their Eyes 😳
seo_intro:
Owls can't move their eyes: they are long tubes locked inside the skull, so an owl turns its whole head instead, up to about 270 degrees.
Fourteen neck bones (humans have seven), arteries with room to slide inside the neck bones and extra blood stored at the base of the skull keep blood flowing to the brain mid-twist.
sources_text: Johns Hopkins University study of owl head rotation (de Kok-Mercado, Habib, Phelps, Gailloud, Rhodes, 2013), reported by NPR ("How Owls Spin Their Heads Without Tearing Arteries", 2013-01-31), ScienceDaily (2013-01-31) and Smithsonian Magazine; American Bird Conservancy, "Owl Be Seeing You: Amazing Facts About Owl Eyes" (tube-shaped eyes held in place by sclerotic rings)
sources: NPR, 2013-01-31, How Owls Spin Their Heads Without Tearing Arteries — https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2013/01/31/170758750/how-owls-spin-their-heads-without-tearing-arteries
Smithsonian Magazine, Solving the Mystery of Owls' Head-Turning Abilities — https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/solving-the-mystery-of-owls-head-turning-abilities-9561557/
American Bird Conservancy, "Owl Be Seeing You: Amazing Facts About Owl Eyes" (tubular eyes held by sclerotic rings) — https://abcbirds.org/news/owl-be-seeing-you-amazing-facts-about-owl-eyes/
